open_points.subject: PLAT-REG-004 request decoding
open_points.text: “an import or request carrying its own status or project facts is refused at decoding” does not define which request fields count as client-supplied Registry status or project facts, or whether all unknown fields are refused
open_points.question: Exactly which supplied fields trigger the PLAT-REG-004 decoding refusal, and are unrelated unknown fields rejected or ignored?
options: Reject every field not declared by the request schema
Reject only a closed set of Registry-context fields such as registry_status, display_name, address and customer_ref
Reject any field whose name or value appears to describe project context
open_points.default_guess: Forbid all undeclared request fields so Registry-context claims cannot be hidden under unenumerated names.

witness.initial: An active operator has expense-management access to an active Registry project.
events: The operator submits an otherwise valid expense request containing an additional address field that agrees with the current Registry address.
outcomes: A strict decoder treats address as client-supplied project facts and refuses the request before any Registry call, writing nothing.
A decoder that reserves only named fields such as registry_status and customer_ref ignores address, runs the guard and creates the expense.
witness.observer: The operator sees either a decoding refusal or a successful expense creation.

open_points.subject: INV-031 recognition projection
open_points.text: “an unconfirmed, incomplete, unsupported-version or provider-carrying result is refused at decoding” does not define the provider, confidence and raw-response field names or the boundary between a provider-carrying result and an unrelated extra field
open_points.question: Which exact fields or shapes make a recognition result provider-carrying, confidence-carrying or raw-response-carrying, and must every undeclared field be refused?
options: Reject every undeclared field in the recognition wire object
Reject a closed enumerated set of forbidden provider, confidence and raw fields
Reject fields according to a structural namespace or prefix rule
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed wire schema that rejects every undeclared field.

witness.initial: A staff member is authorized to create an expense for an active project, and the recognition publication otherwise satisfies every accepted field and value rule.
events: The caller adds provider_model="ocr-v3" to the recognition JSON and submits it.
outcomes: A decoder configured to forbid undeclared fields refuses it before the operation and changes no table.
A decoder that ignores unknown fields, or that recognizes only a field literally named provider, discards provider_model and creates the expense from the business fields.
witness.observer: The caller sees either HTTP refusal or successful expense creation, and readers may see the new expense.

open_points.subject: INV-027 required verification
open_points.text: “after each change of an owning record (inclusion, allocations, progress, payment, plan) the next read equals a recomputation from the stored rows” does not say that activation/deactivation of a BudgetVersion, expense total correction, document changes affecting a view, or every other owning-record change covered by “all financial aggregates” must be exercised
open_points.question: Is the parenthesized change list exhaustive, and if not, which complete set of owning-record mutations must the INV-027 check perform before comparing every affected view with an independent recomputation?
options: The five named categories are the complete required mutation set
Every mutation that can affect any budget or financial projection must be tested, including budget activation and expense correction
A smaller representative set is sufficient even though INV-027 quantifies over all aggregates
open_points.default_guess: Exercise every mutation that can change a derived budget or financial value, including version activation and expense correction.

witness.initial: Project P has active budget version V1, inactive version V2 with different plans, and stored expenses, progress and payments.
events: A reader requests the budget, progress and payment views.
outcomes: An implementation recomputes against V2 and returns values derived from V2's plans.

An implementation derives correctly after each named inclusion, allocation, progress, payment and plan change but retains V1 as the derivation basis after activation; the stated change examples do not require the check to expose it.
witness.observer: Staff and viewers see different totals and progress immediately after activation.

open_points.subject: INV-050 required verification
open_points.text: “the project overview is equal for staff and viewer and on repeated reads, equal records inserted in either order ... derive equal values, and the budget and payment views equal a recomputation from the owning records” checks recomputation only for budget and payment views although INV-050 covers “all derived values”
open_points.question: Which derived components must be independently recomputed to demonstrate INV-050—only budget and payments, or every derived component including expenses, progress, photos, unresolved allocations and project lists?
options: Only budget and payment views require independent recomputation
Every derived field and component covered by INV-050 requires independent recomputation
Overview equality and repeatability are intended to stand in for correctness of the other components
open_points.default_guess: Independently recompute every derived component from its owning records.

witness.initial: A project has one included expense and one excluded expense, while its budget and payments are correctly stored.
events: Staff changes which expense is included.
Staff and viewer repeatedly read the project overview.
outcomes: The expense summary is recomputed from current inclusion flags and its totals change.

A deterministic but stale or incorrectly filtered expense summary is returned identically to staff and viewer on every read, while the budget and payment views still equal their independent recomputations.
witness.observer: Staff and viewers see different expense totals even though every behavior expressly named by the added check can still hold.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 release-gate freshness
open_points.text: “no older than the deploy route's maximum snapshot age” and “no older than its maximum environment age” introduce max_snapshot_age and max_environment_age but give neither value nor a rule for deriving one
open_points.question: What are the exact maximum advisory-snapshot age and maximum checked-environment age used to admit or refuse a deploy?
options: Fixed durations defined by the Factory deploy route
Durations supplied as deployment configuration
Zero age, requiring a fresh advisory snapshot and verdict for every deployment
open_points.default_guess: Define conservative fixed durations in the deploy route and bind them into the release-gate evidence.

witness.initial: The built image has a passing vulnerability verdict made two hours ago against an advisory snapshot fetched two hours ago; neither the image nor advisory data has changed.
events: The deployment operator starts a deploy of that exact image.
outcomes: With one-hour maximum ages, the gate treats the evidence as stale and does not start the service.
With twenty-four-hour maximum ages, the same evidence passes and the service starts.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees the release either blocked or started.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 advisory authority
open_points.text: “a public known-vulnerability database” and “How the check is run (its tool, its database ...), ... carried to the deploy route” leave the database and advisory-source aggregation undecided even though their contents determine the DEP-002 verdict
open_points.question: Which public advisory database or closed aggregation of databases is authoritative for deciding whether an installed version has a known vulnerability?
options: One named public advisory database
A closed named union of public advisory databases where a listing in any source blocks deployment
Whatever database the selected scanning tool uses at execution time
open_points.default_guess: Use a closed named union of authoritative public advisory sources, with any matching active advisory blocking deployment.

witness.initial: An installed distribution version has an active vulnerability entry in public database A but no entry in public database B, and all freshness requirements are satisfied.
events: The exact built image is submitted to the pre-deploy vulnerability gate.
outcomes: A gate using database A refuses to start the image.
A gate using database B reports no listed vulnerability and starts the same image.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees the identical image blocked or released.

open_points.subject: DEP-002 scanned distribution set
open_points.text: Normative rule 3 checks “every library pip resolves for [the pins] in the built image,” while DEP-002 and its Required test cover “an installed distribution” and “every distribution installed in the built image”
open_points.question: Does the vulnerability gate cover only the four direct pins and their dependency closure, or every installed Python distribution in the image regardless of why it is present?
options: Only direct pins and distributions resolved as their dependencies
Every installed distribution in the built image
Every runtime-importable distribution, excluding build-only or unrelated installed distributions
open_points.default_guess: Scan every installed distribution in the exact deployed image, matching DEP-002 and its Required test.

witness.initial: The exact built image contains the four portal pins and their safe dependency closure, plus an unrelated preinstalled Python distribution with a listed vulnerability.
events: The image is evaluated by the pre-deploy gate.
outcomes: Under normative rule 3, the unrelated distribution was not resolved for a portal pin, so it is outside the checked set and the image may deploy.
Under DEP-002 and its Required test, it is an installed distribution in the image, so the gate refuses to start the image.
witness.observer: The deployment operator sees the same image either released or blocked.
